osq_prompt: State the primary focus of Lean Engineering in system lifecycle models. Answer in 1 sentence.
expected_answer: Reducing waste and focusing on value-added activities.

rubric.full_credit: 2 points: The response clearly includes BOTH elements: (a) reducing/eliminating waste (e.g., "reduce waste," "eliminate non-value-added work") AND (b) focusing/emphasizing value-added activities or customer value (e.g., "focus on value-added activities," "maximize customer value"). Examples that earn full credit: "Eliminating non–value-added work to maximize customer value," "Reducing waste while emphasizing value-added activities along the lifecycle."
rubric.partial_credit: 1 point: The response includes ONLY ONE of the two required elements (either waste reduction OR value/value-added focus), or states a close paraphrase that implies only one side. Examples: "Reducing waste and streamlining processes" (no explicit value focus), "Maximizing customer value" (no explicit waste reduction). Mentioning quality/efficiency/streamlining without explicit waste or value earns 0–1 point only if one required element is clearly present.
rubric.no_credit: 0 points: Omits both waste reduction and value-added focus, or contradicts lean principles. Examples: emphasizing speed regardless of quality, prioritizing documentation over implementation, maximizing investment/costs, vague statements like "improve quality" or "accelerate development" without any mention of waste or value.

blooms_justification: The task requires recalling the core definition/focus of Lean Engineering without analysis or application.
